figs.cap: The Line Graph construction. Black vertices and dashed lines correspond the original graph G, while grey vertices and the solid lines correspond to L(G).
The weighted line graph A superimposed to the Hexagonal lattice, for a given orientation, where blue are antiferromagnetic couplings (negative) and red are ferromagnetic (positive).

Mapping of a vertex of degree 4 (given a certain orientation of the spins) in the spin ice formulation of eqn. ( 1 ) to the effective line graph dual of eqn. ( 10 ). The figures shows the equivalent Ising interaction model where black lines are ferromagnetic interactions while with red lines equal to antiferromagnetic interactions. It is possible to see that every single fundamental cycle (the triangles) are frustrated, e.g. the product of the signs of the interactions are always negative.
The coarse graining procedure according to the Krausz partitioning.
